findings.heading: Keep only unique rows
findings.proposition: The translation inserts a translator's note (訳注) asserting that the English sentence is in error and that distinct() removes the SECOND row for "adam", not the first, because the first of a set of duplicates is retained. The English states only that the first row (for "adam") was 100% duplicated and has been removed, and makes no claim that any statement is an error.
findings.reader_consequence: The Japanese reader is told the source text is wrong and learns a row-retention rule about distinct() that the English chapter never states here, so the two language versions teach a different account of which physical row survives de-duplication.

findings.heading: Keep only unique rows
findings.proposition: The translation inserts a second translator's note (訳注：削除されるのは 4 行目) asserting that the row actually deleted in the "amrish" pair is row 4. The English states that row 3 (for "amrish") is the one removed and contains no such correction.
findings.reader_consequence: The Japanese reader concludes that row 4 is removed while the English reader concludes row 3 is removed; a reader cross-checking the printed output or writing code that depends on which record survives gets a different answer depending on the language read.

findings.heading: Roll-up values into one row
findings.proposition: The translation says that if you want to keep NA values you delete `paste0(.x)`. The English says na.omit() removes NA values and that na.omit() itself is the thing to remove, leaving `paste0(.x)` in place.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader who follows the instruction deletes the paste0() call that performs the roll-up, which removes the collapsing step entirely instead of preserving NA values, so the summarise() no longer produces the concatenated one-row-per-group output the section is teaching.

findings.heading: Examine duplicate rows
findings.proposition: The translation states that "these 2 columns" (この 2 列) are 100% duplicates. The English states that the first two ROWS of obs are 100% duplicates; no claim is made about two duplicated columns.
findings.reader_consequence: In a chapter whose whole subject is the difference between evaluating rows and evaluating columns, the reader is told the duplication is between two columns, which inverts the unit of duplication being demonstrated by get_dupes().
